title: Hash-chained audit log
description: Each audit entry includes the hash of the previous entry, forming a chain. Any modification to an earlier entry breaks every later hash, so tampering is detectable by re-verifying the chain. The genesis hash is published so the chain has a trusted starting point. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers each entry committing to the previous hash.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: 5, 2: 10, 3: 25}
N = CFG[LEVEL]
import hashlib
def h(s): return hashlib.sha256(s.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
chain, prev = [], "GENESIS"
for i in range(N):
    prev = h(prev + "|event-%d" % i); chain.append(prev)
ok, prev = True, "GENESIS"
for i, c in enumerate(chain):
    prev = h(prev + "|event-%d" % i)
    if prev != c: ok = False
chain[3] = "tampered"
prev, detected = "GENESIS", False
for i, c in enumerate(chain):
    prev = h(prev + "|event-%d" % i)
    if prev != c: detected = True
print("entries:", N, "| clean chain verifies:", ok, "| tamper detected:", detected)
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Merkle-tree batch attestation
description: Audit entries are batched into a Merkle tree and only the root hash is published or timestamped. Any single entry can be proven included with a logarithmic-size proof, without revealing the other entries. Batching makes external attestation cheap. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers batching entries into a Merkle tree.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: 4, 2: 8, 3: 16}
N = CFG[LEVEL]
import hashlib
def h(s): return hashlib.sha256(s.encode()).hexdigest()
leaves = [h("entry-%d" % i) for i in range(N)]
lvl = leaves
while len(lvl) > 1:
    lvl = [h(lvl[i] + lvl[i + 1]) for i in range(0, len(lvl), 2)]
root = lvl[0]
print("entries:", N, "| merkle root:", root[:16], "| proof size: %d hashes" % (N.bit_length()))
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Append-only enforcement
description: Once sealed, audit entries cannot be modified or deleted: the storage layer rejects writes to sealed ranges. Corrections are new entries that supersede, never edits. Append-only is enforced in code and, where available, in the storage medium itself. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers rejecting writes to sealed entries.

title: Independent timestamping
description: Log checkpoints are sent to an independent timestamping authority which returns a signed receipt binding the hash to a wall-clock time. Even if local clocks are manipulated, the external receipts prove when entries existed. Receipts are stored with the log. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers external signed timestamp receipts.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: 2, 2: 4, 3: 6}
import hashlib, time
receipts = []
for i in range(CFG[LEVEL]):
    digest = hashlib.sha256(("batch-%d" % i).encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
    receipts.append({"digest": digest, "ts": 1761000000 + i * 3600, "by": "tsa-example"})
print("timestamped batches:", len(receipts), "| first:", receipts[0])
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Gap detection
description: Audit entries carry monotonic sequence numbers; any gap in the sequence proves entries are missing. Gap detection runs continuously and alerts immediately, because missing audit entries are as serious as altered ones. Expected gaps (archival) are declared in advance. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers monotonic sequence numbers.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: [1, 2, 3, 4], 2: [1, 2, 4, 5], 3: [1, 3, 7]}
seq = CFG[LEVEL]
gaps = [ (seq[i] + 1, seq[i+1] - 1) for i in range(len(seq) - 1) if seq[i+1] - seq[i] > 1 ]
print("sequence:", seq, "| gaps:", gaps or ["none"])
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.
